exact text. Keys and strings, which never have pending text, use the
unchecked get_string_token(). Input read through a window into a stream

refill the window.

Lohmann","email":"mail@nlohmann.me","date":"2026-10-21T10:26:46Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-10-21T10:26:46Z"},"message":"Accumulate number digits while scanning them (#5851)

* Accumulate number digits while scanning them

The contiguous number fast path validated a token byte by byte, copied it
into token_buffer, and then converted it in out-of-line functions that
scanned the digits a second time: parse_float_native() called
parse_float_significand(), which returned its result through memory and
called std::any_of (out of line with GCC) twice per number, and
parse_integer_signed() divided by ten on every digit for its overflow check.

scan_number_bulk_contiguous() now accumulates the significand while it
validates the digits, eight at a time where at least eight bytes remain
(is_eight_digits() and parse_eight_digits(), after fast_float). Floats with
at most 19 digits go straight to decimal_to_float(); integers with at most
18 digits are stored without an overflow check (a narrower number type
still rejects values that do not round-trip). Longer tokens take the
existing path. has_nonzero_digit() is a plain loop and
parse_float_significand() is always inlined, which helps that path.

Signed-off-by: Niels Lohmann <mail@nlohmann.me>

* Skip the digit accumulation checks without exceptions

The section compares error messages from both lexer paths and parses
out-of-range numbers, so it does not compile (the caught exception does not
exist) and would abort with JSON_NOEXCEPTION.

Signed-off-by: Niels Lohmann <mail@nlohmann.me>

* Share the significant-digit loop of the integer part and the fraction

Signed-off-by: Niels Lohmann <mail@nlohmann.me>
